subject: NextHealth tenant activation: initial access & API key plan

Subject: NextHealth tenant activation: initial access & API key plan

Hi Samira,

Great to meet you on the call today — excited to get NextHealth into a staging tenant so your team can start smoke-testing the integration. I wanted to capture the initial actions we'll take for tenant/org setup and access provisioning so we have a clear kickoff. Please review and confirm any specifics we should change.

Goal: Create NextHealth staging workspace, seed admin project, create service accounts + API keys, and invite initial users (SRE, App Eng, CS).

Planned steps (first pass):
- Create org "nexthealth-staging" and an admin project called "nexthealth-core".
- Seed two API keys: one long-lived admin key (rotated quarterly) and one ephemeral key for CI/CD (90-day TTL).
- Provision service account "svc-nexthealth-ingest" for ingestion pipeline; grant roles: project.admin (limited), svc-invoke for runtime.
- Invite users: raj.patel@nexthealth.io (SRE), samira@nexthealth.io (product lead), it-admin@nexthealth.io (IT).
- Ask IT for SSO SAML metadata or Okta domain to enable SSO; if no SSO, we'll enable invite-only accounts.

Open questions for you:
1) Who is the canonical IT contact for KMS/BYOK decisions?
2) Does NextHealth require BYOK / HSM integration for keys? If yes, share KMS provider (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or vendor).
3) Any IP egress allowlists we should pre-provision?

Timeline: we can provision the staging workspace tomorrow and run a technical kickoff on Friday morning (30–45 min) to walk through API key rotation, service account permissions, and sample requests.

I've attached a starter onboarding checklist and a lightweight project/role matrix for you to review. If that looks good, Ben (solutions) and Monica (implementation) will own the technical kickoff.

Thanks —

Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Attachments: onboard-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), project-role-matrix.md (text)

- We are currently evaluating BYOK but defaulting to Redwood-managed keys for staging. For production we'll likely request BYOK.

Hi team — adding a short technical checklist and a few implementation notes so Raj has something tangible before the kickoff: 

Required items (we'll need these during the call or immediately after):
- SSO: SAML metadata XML or Okta org admin invite (nexthealth.okta.com). We import SSO and map the email attribute to Redwood username.
- KMS: if BYOK later, we support AWS KMS and GCP KMS (customer-managed keys). For staging, Redwood-managed keys are fine. If you want an HSM-backed KMS, note that procurement lead time is ~2–3 weeks.
- Service accounts: recommend names and roles:
  * svc-nexthealth-ingest — role: ingest.service (can write to ingestion queue)
  * svc-nexthealth-batch — role: batch.runner (for offline jobs)
  * svc-nexthealth-admin — role: org.admin (restricted to admin tasks)
- API key naming convention: nexthealth-stg-admin-YYYYMMDD, nexthealth-stg-ci-YYYYMMDD. We seed keys using an ephemeral vault path to make rotation safe.
- Key rotation: we recommend quarterly rotation for admin keys; CI keys with a 90-day TTL. We provide rotation scripts and a webhook you can call after rotation for downstream tooling.

Audit/logging note: Admin actions and key events are logged to the account audit stream and retained for 365 days by default on our Dedicated and Private options; hosted tiers retain 90 days unless you add the extended-audit add-on. We will include a pointer to the audit export (S3/GCS) in the deliverables.

Attachments referenced: api-key-warmup-instructions.pdf (short how-to), kms-integration-guide.md (notes for BYOK).

I'll upload the example rotation script to the hub and share the link in the calendar invite. Looking forward to Friday.

Monica Patel
